title: Rank bug closures on lifecycle evidence, not merge tiebreak fields
context: Bug closures only change status; provenance and date fields unchanged. Merge tiebreaking used lexicographic order on these static fields, so unfixed copies won because null > sha and 'open' > 'fixed'. Teams silently got reopened bugs after merges.
decision: Switched conflict resolution from lexicographic tiebreaking to one-way lifecycle evidence. Bug closures now survive merges; genuine reopens still take precedence.
consequences: Closed bugs no longer revert to open during merge
Bug status is now stable across merge operations
Merge conflict resolution no longer uses fields unrelated to the actual change
alternatives_rejected: Change tiebreak field priority (brittle, only masks symptom)
Block merges involving bug closures (too restrictive)
Update provenance/date on closure (rewrites timestamps, obscures intent)
